title: Synergistic effects of traffic-related air pollution and exposure to violence on urban asthma etiology.
ehr_evidence: Data collection and analysis for the nitrogen dioxide passive network and violence exposure assessment were supported by the Massachusetts Port Authority (P.B.R.) and K08 HL 04187 (R.J.W.)
summary: This study examined the role of exposure to violence (ETV) in altering susceptibility to traffic-related air pollution (NO2) in asthma etiology among children in East Boston, Massachusetts.
key_findings: A 1-SD increase in NO2 exposure was associated with an elevated risk of asthma solely among children with above-median ETV (OR = 1.63; 95% CI, 1.14–2.33).
Among lifetime residents, the association between NO2 and asthma was magnified (OR = 2.40; 95% CI, 1.48–3.88).
population: 413 children in East Boston, Massachusetts, recruited in 1987-1993
limitations: reliance on questionnaire data for violence exposure
small sample size for investigating multiplicative effects
